# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment

## Description

Resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps between
current Tech Preview quality and the GA bar is not yet known — TP feedback is
scattered across support tickets and no systematic GA-readiness assessment
has been done. This investigation produces the definitive GA scope that the
API stability, hardening, and support-posture work is sized against, and
determines whether that downstream work proceeds as estimated or must be
rewritten.

## Scope

- Inventory the gaps between current TP quality and the GA bar across the
  four dimensions named by the strategy: API stability, upgrade paths, scale
  limits, and error handling.
- Consolidate and triage TP feedback scattered across support tickets into
  the gap inventory.
- For each identified gap, record severity, affected surface, and a
  remediation estimate.
- Produce the definitive GA scope document (what is in and out of GA) and
  obtain stakeholder ratification of the GA bar it encodes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the current TP distribution, when the published API surface is
  examined against the GA bar, then every API-stability gap is inventoried
  with severity and affected surface.
- Given the last two TP releases, when their upgrade paths are examined, then
  upgrade-path gaps against the GA bar are inventoried.
- Given current deployment scales and error-handling behavior, then
  scale-limit and error-handling gaps are inventoried.
- Given TP feedback scattered across support tickets, when consolidated, then
  recurring quality themes are triaged into the gap inventory.
- The definitive GA scope document exists, covers all four dimensions, and is
  ratified by the owning team and stakeholders; measured by the downstream
  stability, hardening, and support-posture work being scopeable from the
  document without re-deriving the analysis.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current
  TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error
  handling), producing the definitive GA scope.

# API stability guarantee for the published Llama Stack API surface

## Description

Delivers the API stability guarantee required for GA: the published API
surface carries versioned APIs, a deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade
path from the last two TP releases. The concrete stability and upgrade-path
work is scoped by the ratified GA scope produced by the GA-readiness
assessment — until that assessment lands, the size of this work is an
estimate, and its scope is rewritten to the definitive GA scope.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface of the Llama Stack distribution
  (OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and distribution interfaces).
- Define and publish the API deprecation policy: how APIs are versioned,
  how deprecation is signaled, and removal timelines across releases.
- Implement and test the upgrade path from each of the last two TP releases.
- Close the API-stability and upgrade-path gaps identified by the
  GA-readiness assessment's inventory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the published API surface, when changes are made, then APIs carry
  version identifiers and breaking changes follow the published deprecation
  policy.
- The deprecation policy is published and covers versioning, deprecation
  notice, and removal timelines.
- Given a distribution running each of the last two TP releases, when
  upgraded through the supported upgrade path, then the upgrade completes
  successfully and previously working API usage remains functional —
  demonstrated by tests.
- All API-stability and upgrade-path gaps assigned to the GA scope for this
  surface are closed; measured by the assessment's gap inventory items for
  those dimensions being resolved.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned
  APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP
  releases.

# Production support posture for Llama Stack

## Description

Establishes the production support posture required for GA: documented SLO
targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration matrix. Enterprise
customers will not build production applications on a component without
these commitments. The posture content is aligned to the ratified GA scope
produced by the GA-readiness assessment — until that assessment lands, the
supported configurations and quality bar are estimates, and the posture
content is rewritten to the definitive GA scope.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA distribution: measurable
  availability and reliability targets as appropriate for the component.
- Define the backport policy: which releases receive fixes and for how long.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix — the providers,
  deployment configurations, and integration combinations validated as
  supported at GA.
- Align all posture content with the ratified GA scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets are documented, measurable, and consistent with the ratified GA
  scope.
- The backport policy is documented and states the supported releases and fix
  duration.
- Every configuration listed in the supported configuration matrix is
  validated as supported — configurations involving the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration are listed only with the TrustyAI team's validation evidence
  for the integration; no unvalidated configuration is listed.
- The support posture is reviewed and accepted by support stakeholders;
  measured by sign-off on the published posture artifacts.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P0): Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets,
  backport policy, and supported configuration matrix.

# TrustyAI safety guardrails as a supported integration in GA Llama Stack distributions

## Description

Promotes the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration from an experimental flag
to a supported, documented integration in GA Llama Stack distributions — the
distribution side of the GA guardrails requirement. The integration already
exists experimentally; this epic changes its support status and default
packaging in GA distributions and documents it at the supported level. The
TrustyAI team validates and commits support for the integration in their own
workstream, running in parallel.

## Scope

- Remove the experimental flag status of the TrustyAI guardrails integration
  in the distribution's provider configuration; GA distributions carry the
  integration as supported rather than experimental.
- Follow the distribution's existing provider-plugin configuration pattern
  for declaring the integration supported.
- Document the integration at the supported level: how it is configured,
  enabled, and what support it carries — replacing experimental and Tech
  Preview labeling in the integration's documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a GA Llama Stack distribution with the TrustyAI guardrails
  integration configured, the safety guardrails function without any
  experimental opt-in flag.
- Given a distribution upgraded from a TP release that carried the
  experimental integration, the guardrails integration remains functional
  under the supported configuration.
- The integration documentation describes configuration and support status
  with no experimental or Tech Preview labeling; measured by documentation
  review against the shipped configuration.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P1): Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions.

The TrustyAI side of the GA guardrails requirement: validate the TrustyAI
safety-guardrails integration against Llama Stack GA distributions and commit
TrustyAI support for it. TrustyAI itself is already a GA component; the work

- Validate the TrustyAI guardrails integration with Llama Stack GA
  distributions across the supported configurations — the
  TrustyAI-integration entries of the supported configuration matrix,
  published as part of the production support posture, are backed by this
  validation.
- Characterize the integration's failure behavior — what happens to guarded
  workloads when the TrustyAI service is unavailable or degraded — and
  document the supported behavior.
- Remediate TrustyAI-side compatibility findings surfaced by validation, or
  document mitigations where remediation falls outside this scope.
- Confirm the TrustyAI support posture for the integration as supported (not
  experimental).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a Llama Stack GA distribution configured with TrustyAI guardrails,
  the integration passes validation in every supported configuration.
- Given the TrustyAI service becoming unavailable or degraded, the
  integration's behavior is characterized and documented, and matches the
  documented supported-integration behavior.
- All TrustyAI-side compatibility findings are remediated or carry documented
  mitigations; measured by a validation report with every finding
  dispositioned.
- TrustyAI's support status for the integration is confirmed as supported.
- Coordination with the supported configuration matrix: every configuration
  involving the TrustyAI guardrails integration that is listed as supported
  in the matrix published as part of the production support posture is
  covered by this epic's validation, and no such configuration is listed
  without it.

user flow, and retains an administrator disable path as the rollback for the
default change.

- Change the Llama Stack management feature-flag default in the Dashboard to
  enabled for entitled clusters, following the Dashboard's per-component
  feature-flag configuration pattern.
- Remove the Tech Preview opt-in gate from the user flow.

# Llama Stack GA hardening for scale limits and error handling

## Description

Delivers the third co-equal GA requirement from the strategy's problem
statement: closing the quality gaps that Tech Preview status currently
excuses. The GA-readiness assessment inventories those gaps across four
dimensions; the API-stability and upgrade-path dimensions are closed by the
API stability workstream, while this epic closes the remaining two — scale
limits and error handling. The concrete gap set is scoped by the ratified GA
scope produced by the GA-readiness assessment: until that assessment lands,
the size of the hardening work is an estimate, and its scope is rewritten to
the definitive GA scope.

## Scope

- Close the scale-limit gaps identified by the GA-readiness assessment's
  inventory, so the distribution meets the GA bar at the scales the ratified
  GA scope designates as supported.
- Close the error-handling gaps identified by the inventory, so error
  reporting, failure behavior, and recovery meet the GA quality bar.
- For every scale-limit and error-handling gap in the inventory, remediate
  it or record its disposition under the ratified GA scope (in or out of
  GA), keyed to the severity and affected surface recorded at inventory
  time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the scale-limit gaps inventoried by the GA-readiness assessment,
  when the distribution is exercised at the scales the ratified GA scope
  designates as supported, then the inventoried scale-limit gaps no longer
  reproduce, demonstrated by tests.
- Given the error-handling gaps inventoried by the GA-readiness assessment,
  when the affected failure conditions are exercised, then errors are
  handled and reported to the GA bar — the inventoried error-handling gaps
  no longer reproduce, demonstrated by tests.
- Every scale-limit and error-handling gap from the assessment's inventory
  is remediated or explicitly dispositioned out of the GA scope by the
  ratified GA scope document; measured by each gap inventory item in those
  two dimensions carrying a resolution.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale
  limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. This epic
  closes the scale-limit and error-handling dimensions of that inventory —
  the problem statement's requirement to close the quality gaps that TP
  status currently excuses.
